newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zairean peace talks on track - South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Zairean peace talks on track - South Africa.

text.p: The South African government confirmed on Thursday that Zairean peace talks would go ahead in Cape Town, but threw a news blackout over the meeting.
"The talks are going on, but we are not releasing any details," said Parks Mankahlana, spokesman for President Nelson Mandela.

Officials in Cape Town declined to give any details of the proposed meeting between rebel leader Laurent Kabila and Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's envoy, his nephew and security adviser, Ngbanda Nzambo Ko Ayumba.
"We are still busy with the logistical arrangements," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Pieter Swanepoel of the meeting expected to take place later on Thursday.
He declined to comment on President Nelson Mandela's statement on Wednesday that South Africa had sent an aircraft to fetch Kabila from Kigali or that Ngbanda was "in the region".

A diplomat involved in the arrangements said both sides in the escalating Zairean conflict had been surprised by Mandela's disclosure of the planned meeting when he responded to a question during an informal news conference on Wednesday.
